title: Connect to Databricks
text: spark_connect_databricks() reads DATABRICKS_HOST DATABRICKS_TOKEN, connects workspace’s serverless compute: spark_version() reports Spark version Databricks runtime behind session. Serverless compute starts session connects, first query can take seconds . plain Spark Connect: TLS port 443, token bearer token, x-databricks-session-id header carrying session id. Without header, server answers “Invalid compute mode headers”. connection spark_connect():
code: con <- spark_connect_databricks() spark_version(con) host <- sub("^https://", "", Sys.getenv("DATABRICKS_HOST")) session <- as.character(zuid::uuid(version = 4))  con <- spark_connect(   sprintf("sc://%s:443/;use_ssl=true", host),   token = Sys.getenv("DATABRICKS_TOKEN"),   session_id = session,   headers = c("x-databricks-session-id" = session) )

text: spark_fetch() returns result Arrow stream rather data frame. Code consumes Arrow can take without rows becoming R vectors first. DuckDB one consumer: summary computed Spark, joined DuckDB table exists locally. DuckDB’s R package registers Arrow data arrow package, stream converted arrow RecordBatchReader first. code: library(DBI) invisible(loadNamespace("nanoarrow"))  totals <- spark_sql(con, "   SELECT id % 7 AS weekday, count(*) AS orders, sum(id % 100) / 100 AS total   FROM range(1000000)   GROUP BY id % 7 ")  local <- dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(shared_home = FALSE)) duckdb::duckdb_register_arrow(   local, "spark_totals",   arrow::as_record_batch_reader(spark_fetch(totals)) )  dbWriteTable(local, "days", data.frame(   weekday = 0:6,   name = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun") ))  dbGetQuery(local, "   SELECT d.name, t.orders, t.total   FROM spark_totals t JOIN days d USING (weekday)   ORDER BY weekday ") #>   name orders    total #> 1  Mon 142858 70714.71 #> 2  Tue 142857 70714.29 #> 3  Wed 142857 70713.86 #> 4  Thu 142857 70714.43 #> 5  Fri 142857 70714.00 #> 6  Sat 142857 70714.57 #> 7  Sun 142857 70714.14 dbDisconnect(local, shutdown = TRUE) spark_disconnect(con)

title: Get started with zuspark
text: spark_collect() runs query returns one data frame. runs every time, result always current. Values R can’t hold exactly, BIGINT beyond 2^53, error default. lossy chooses exact text widened type instead. spark_fetch() returns result Arrow stream instead, code consumes Arrow directly, spark_execute() runs statement effect, returning number rows produced.
code: spark_collect(q) #>   id twice s #> 1  0     0 0 #> 2  1     2 1 #> 3  2     4 2 #> 4  3     6 3 #> 5  4     8 4 big <- spark_sql(con, "SELECT 9007199254740993 AS id") conditionMessage(tryCatch(spark_collect(big), error = identity)) #> [1] "Column `id` (Arrow format `l`) can't be converted to R exactly: row 1 holds 9007199254740993. Load zuint to read it exactly, or use `lossy = \"character\"` for its exact text, or `lossy = \"allow\"` to accept the loss." spark_collect(big, lossy = "character") #>                 id #> 1 9007199254740993 spark_collect(big, lossy = "allow") #>             id #> 1 9.007199e+15 stream <- spark_fetch(q) zuarrow::arrow_schema(stream) #> <zuarrow_schema> struct<id: int64, twice: int64, s: string> n <- spark_execute(con, "SELECT * FROM range(1000000)") n #> [1] 1e+06
